Alexandroupoli Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Alexandroupoli, Greece

Not demolished. A small Jewish community existed in Alexandroupoli from the early 20th century, running a school and numbering 48 families by 1912; it dwindled in the 1920s and faced financial distress in the 1930s, reaching 165 (of 15,472 total residents) by 1940. Bulgarian rule from April 1941 restricted Jewish movement and imposed severe anti-Jewish measures on the 197-member community; on March 3-4, 1943, Jews were rounded up and taken to a Bulgarian camp, then transported via Vienna to Treblinka on March 19. Of 15 Alexandroupoli Jews who survived the war, none remained in the town after 1960. This cemetery was founded in the early 20th century.
